value.title: Cross-model review R4 — 132-spawn-reports-bind @ 3eeb232a
value.note: VERDICT: APPROVE — no blocking findings. Two items should be ANSWERED before the PR (N9, N10); neither holds the merge. Focused delta review of 46a2d862..3eeb232a covering prime's two required fixes, with re-adjudication of the carried set. BOTH PRIME FIXES LAND CORRECTLY: the refusal envelope now carries structured `details` with the exact five ruled fields, asserted by SHAPE (details.len()==5, parsed as JSON) rather than by prose match — which closes both R003 and the AC-coverage hole behind it via the new G7/AC6; and pane-absence terminalization now requires an explicit socket-unreachable result, with can_deliver's Err correctly routed to release-and-surface BEFORE the terminalize check, so the unknown-versus-observed-negative trap I flagged at the ack is avoided. That distinction has now been drawn correctly three times in this plan (actual_model, pane inventory, socket reachability). FRESH GATE RECEIPTS taken by this reviewer at 3eeb232a: `cargo test --workspace` EXIT 0, 612 passed, 0 failed; `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` EXIT 0; `cargo test -p pij-daemon pointer::worker::tests` 29 passed, 0 failed — all three matching the PM's reported figures. TWO NEW FINDINGS, both MINOR: N9, a pre-bind command-injection policy divergence introduced as a side effect of the reorder, with no comment and no test; and N10, the production-copy proof was not re-run against this code, provable from its own recorded reason strings. AC VERDICTS: AC1a, AC1b, AC2, AC3, AC4, AC6 TRUE; AC5 TRUE on the evidence now properly split in prod-copy-proof.md, with the claim-text over-claim noted at N11. FOUR CARRIED ITEMS CLOSED THIS ROUND: N3, N4, N6, N8.

value.finding: NEW, and the only item I want an answer on before the PR. The `if recipient.proc.is_none() { release_or_backoff }` check MOVED from above the command branch to below it, so a COMMAND message addressed to an UNBOUND recipient whose pane exists is no longer deferred — it now reaches fresh_injection_verdict and submit_command_claim and is typed into the pane of a client that has never registered. Old order was tombstone, Hold, pane-none, pane-absent, PROC-NONE, command, body; new order is tombstone, Hold, pane-none, pane-absent, COMMAND, proc-none, body. This diverges the drain worker from the system's own enqueue-time policy: crates/core/src/delivery.rs route() returns Queue(QueueReason::PreBind) for any recipient with proc.is_none() and does not branch on command, so a pre-bind command is queued by policy and, until this commit, was held by the worker for the same reason. The pre-bind deferral is now enforced only incidentally by the composer-recognition gate — a POLITENESS check standing in for a BINDING check, which is the same category error the plan-117 comment named in the opposite direction ('an absence check standing where a liveness check belongs'). I cannot demonstrate harm: fresh_injection_verdict is a partial backstop and will usually refuse a booting client that has not drawn a composer. But the window between a harness drawing its composer and completing pij registration is real, and typing a command into it is the known composer-clobber hazard. The change carries no comment and no test, and the suite is green either way, so nothing records that a documented policy moved. Smallest fix if unintended: restore the proc check above the command branch. If intended: say so in a comment and add a test asserting a pre-bind command is injected on purpose.
value.receipt: HEAD crates/daemon/src/pointer/worker.rs lines 225-241 versus the same function at 46a2d862; crates/core/src/delivery.rs:201-203 route() PreBind rule, which does not branch on msg.command. No test in the 46a2d862..3eeb232a diff covers a command to a proc-none recipient.

value.finding: NEW. AC5's production receipt was NOT re-run against the R4 code, and its own text proves it: every sample_reasons entry reads 'is absent from tmux list-panes -a; not retried', while the shipped code at HEAD emits 'is absent from tmux list-panes -a AND NO SOCKET IS REACHABLE; not retried'. The message string is the tell — the recorded run came from the pre-socket-probe binary. The outcome is very probably unchanged, because UdsTransport::can_deliver short-circuits to Ok(false) for any harness that is not Claude and the sampled seats are omp, so those 72 rows would terminalize identically. But the document asserts a production result for a binary that is not the one being merged, and does not say so; and the socket probe is exactly the new per-claim I/O that a 72-row, 21-rows-on-one-seat production run would have exercised. Smallest fix: one sentence stating the run predates the socket-probe change and why it still holds, or re-run the cadence.

value.finding: FIXED, and fixed in the shape I asked for rather than the cheap one. Envelope gains an additive `details: Option<serde_json::Value>` and spawn_failure populates the exact five ruled fields as STRUCTURED DATA, not a reason string that happens to contain them. The AC gap I escalated to prime is closed too: G7 and AC6 are new, and AC6's claim is about SHAPE, so the coverage hole that let content-only ACs miss this cannot recur. The test parses the object and asserts details.len() == 5 plus each field, rather than grepping meta — which is precisely the failure mode that would have reproduced the gap it closes. `bound` is derived from seat.proc.is_some(), so the model-mismatch path correctly reports bound:true with a refusal (the seat IS bound, the model did not match) while the child-exit and timeout paths report bound:false.
value.receipt: crates/core/src/model.rs Envelope::details; crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs spawn_failure; crates/daemon/src/http/tests.rs asserts details.len()==5 with dispatched/bound/pane/pid/reason parsed as JSON; plan.dd.md G7 and AC6.

value.finding: RESOLVED by prime's ruling, and implemented with the correct tri-state — which is the third time this plan has had to separate 'unknown' from 'observed negative' and the third time it has been done right. can_deliver's three answers are all distinguished: Ok(true) exempts the recipient from terminalization and delivers over the socket without tmux; Ok(false) terminalizes; Err releases the body and returns the error BEFORE the terminalize check is reached, so an unproven negative can never be treated as proof. The probe is correctly skipped when it cannot matter (command messages, which can_deliver refuses anyway, and proc-none recipients, for which discover() has no pid). Both witnesses are discriminating: missing_pane_with_reachable_socket_delivers_instead_of_terminalizing asserts actual delivery plus Outcome::Done plus zero retries, and unknown_socket_reachability_retries_and_surfaces_the_error asserts retry at Duration::ZERO, live_len 1, ZERO acks (so it cannot pass by terminalizing) and the visible error. The update of a_missing_pane_terminalizes... from FakeTransport::reachable() to unreachable() is a correct test repair, not a weakening: terminalization is that test's subject and it must now arrange unreachability to reach it.

It now states that a successful inventory makes the vanished recipient terminal, that this test proves the live recipient behind it still delivers in the same pass, and it points at pane_inventory_failure_is_deferred_while_recipient_work_continues for the systemic tmux-error half. The institutional memory is preserved and now describes the mechanism the code actually uses.

value.finding: FIXED, and better than I asked for. The proof now carries an explicit Evidence split table naming all six states with the receipt for each, and states plainly that production contained no tombstoned pending rows so production proves only the pane-absent/unreachable case while the tombstone and unknown states are unit-proven. That is per-claim evidence grading rather than one label over a mixed section, and it is exactly what stops the 72-to-0 headline from carrying claims it did not test.

value.finding: NEW, small but worth a line because AC rows are what get quoted downstream. AC5's claim text still reads 'zero pending delivery rows to tombstoned or pane-absent recipients', which now OVER-CLAIMS relative to the ruled behaviour: after prime's fix a pane-absent recipient with a reachable socket is deliberately NOT terminalized. G7 states the qualifier and the prod-copy Evidence split table handles it correctly, but the AC row itself does not. Smallest fix: add 'and socket-unreachable' to AC5's claim.

value.finding: NEW, NIT. `socket_available.expect("bound body probes socket reachability")` puts a panic in the delivery hot path. It is sound today — the command branch has returned and proc.is_some() was just checked, so the Option is necessarily Some — but the invariant is held by two checks sitting several lines apart in a function that has now been reordered twice in three rounds, and N9 is evidence that this ordering does move. A panic here kills the drain task rather than deferring an error. Cheap alternative: match the None arm into release_or_backoff.

OPEN BUT IMPROVED. The CLI now propagates the daemon's structured `details` through retype_envelope and spawn_cli_response rather than discarding it, so the whole failure path is the daemon's own answer end to end. The original finding survives only on the SUCCESS path, where spawn_cli_response still drops SpawnResponse's dispatched/bound/pid and recomputes them from the descriptor, with dispatched hardcoded true client-side.

value.finding: OPEN AND FURTHER BOUNDED, twice now. Terminalization already required a successful inventory after R3; it now additionally requires an explicit socket-unreachable result. A revive-window loss therefore needs pane absence AND a proven-dead socket AND a drain tick inside the window, which is a materially smaller target than the R2 version. The residual is unchanged in kind: fail_claim is terminal and the check applies to bound seats.
CONFIRMED OPEN, unchanged across all four rounds. Spawn evidence files under temp_dir()/pij-rs-spawn/ leak on the no_wait path and on every revive.
CARRIED FORWARD, unchanged. requested_model_matches is still called with actual_observed hardcoded true in the spawn wait loop.

RESOLVED. Prime confirmed paneless pull ownership as deliberate, and it is now witnessed rather than merely asserted: paneless_pull_consumer_keeps_ownership_of_its_queue_row exists and the prod-copy Evidence split table lists the paneless non-tombstoned state with that test as its receipt. The exclusion is a documented design position, not an oversight.
